messages:
Maya: Quick RFC follow-up — re: dedicated GPU pool autoscaling surface. Do we split the autoscaler into a lightweight admission operator + a separate optimizer service, or keep a single monolithic operator that owns scaling, prewarm, and backoff?
Ashwin: My gut: split. Operator should be minimal (admit/reject + stable lease), optimizer lives in control-plane and can iterate fast.
Samira: Split helps iteration but increases runtime handoff complexity. How do we guarantee consistency during rollouts? race conditions on leases are scary.
Liam: If we split, define a clear idempotent contract: Admission API returns Lease{id, expires_at, soft_flag} and Optimizer can extend/renew. All actions must be idempotent.
Maya: Agree on contract idea. Also need telemetry signals for optimizer: live inflight, observed queue depth, startup latency histogram, prewarm success rate. Without those the optimizer will be blind.
Ashwin: Telemetry can be emitted by operator as aggregated metrics + per-tenant samples. We should avoid high-cardinality logs. Proposed metrics: tenant_inflight, tenant_queue, prewarm_failures_5m, start_latency_p50_p95.
Samira: We need safety fallbacks: if control-plane optimizer is unavailable, operator must switch to a safe local policy (bounded growth + cooldown). Otherwise customer UX will break during control-plane deploys.
Liam: Yep. Fallback sketch: operator keeps a local PID-ish controller with conservative gains and rate limits; optimizer provides delta adjustments when healthy.
Maya: What about API surface? Keep Kubernetes CRD for desired capacity, operator exposes HTTP admission endpoints for transient lease requests. Optimizer calls admission endpoint and monitors leases.
Ashwin: CRD for long-lived reservations + admission endpoint for short-lived bursts seems reasonable. We should avoid exposing raw scaling decisions in CRD to prevent drift.
Samira: Migration plan idea: start with optimizer writing suggested headroom into CRD (opt-in), operator reads CRD for a few customers, then flip gradully to direct admission. Rollback path: optimizer writes null or empty to indicate withdraw.
Maya: Ops concerns: debugging cross-service interactions will need good traces (trace-id propagated from optimizer->admission->node). Add that to tracing checklist.
OrchBot: reminder: autoscaler-alert 2026-03-18 09:12 UTC — prewarm failure spike detected in canary cluster.
Liam: Good call. That incident highlights need for prewarm_failures metric + automated rollback if prewarm rate > threshold.
Ashwin: Action items: 1) Draft admission API proto + idempotency semantics, 2) Define telemetry contract and sampling budget, 3) Prototype local fallback controller. I'll take (1). Maya take (2). Samira take (3).
Maya: Sounds good. I'll open a short RFC update with the proto sketch and metric list. Ping me if you want to pair on the traces. :thumbsup:
Samira: I'll start the fallback controller PoC and add tests for race scenarios.
Liam: I'll wire a small demo that shows optimizer -> admission -> operator renewal flow.
Maya: Great — let's sync in the next eng-runtime sync and mark this issue as blocking the dedicated pool canary rollout.
Ashwin: +1
Samira: +1
Liam: +1
OrchBot: deploybot: created issue INC-5421 for canary prewarm alert investigation.
